paper.central_claim: ERL reflects on single-attempt task trajectories and outcomes to write trigger-conditioned heuristics into a persistent pool, retrieves the most relevant ones with an LLM at test time and injects them into the agent's system prompt; on Gaia2 (Search and Execution) it improves success by 7.8 points over a ReAct baseline, outperforms ExpeL and AutoGuide, selective retrieval is essential, and heuristics transfer better than raw few-shot trajectories.
paper.title: Experiential Reflective Learning for Self-Improving LLM Agents

evidence.quote: ERL reflects on task trajectories and outcomes to generate heuristics, capturing actionable lessons that transfer across tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Central operation: outcome-grounded reflection into reusable heuristics (text store).

evidence.quote: Both methods require multiple rollouts per task to construct contrastive trajectory pairs, an assumption that breaks down in practical agent deployment where tasks cannot be retried.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap against nearest neighbors ExpeL and AutoGuide (retries / paired trajectories).

evidence.quote: After each task, the agent reflects on this experience to generate a structured heuristic containing: (1) an analysis identifying what led to success or failure, and (2) a learned guideline with explicit trigger conditions and recommended actions
evidence.support_explanation: Heuristic format; one heuristic per task, from a single trajectory and its binary outcome; no admission test.

evidence.quote: An LLM analyzes the new task, decomposes it into potential sub-tasks and action steps, and scores each stored heuristic for relevance.
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval is an LLM scoring pass over the whole pool at task start.

evidence.quote: we accumulate heuristics on 8 universes (112 execution / 132 search tasks) and evaluate on 2 held-out test universes (48 / 28 tasks).
evidence.support_explanation: Accumulation and test streams are disjoint universes; test set is 76 tasks, run 3 times.

evidence.quote: isolated data partitions that expose identical applications and tools but contain completely disjoint information
evidence.support_explanation: Universe structure is the basis for contamination-free evaluation (shared tools, different data).

evidence.quote: ERL achieves a 56.1% overall success rate, an improvement of +7.8% over the ReAct baseline and +5.2% over the strongest prior method (ExpeL at 50.9%).
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result on 2 test universes (GPT-5-mini agent).
Execution / Search / Overall success (%). AutoGuide is higher than ERL on Search (61.9 vs 60.7) but below the baseline on Execution (39.6 vs 43.1).

evidence.quote: Ablations: no retrieval 44.4 63.1 53.8 embedding retrieval 50.7 56.0 53.3 only failures 50.0 67.9 58.9 only successes 52.1 47.6 49.9
evidence.support_explanation: The 'no retrieval' row is random heuristic selection (best random config 53.8), embedding retrieval 53.3, failures-only 58.9, successes-only 49.9.

evidence.quote: We sample a subset of training tasks matching the test set distribution (48 execution, 28 search).
evidence.support_explanation: ExpeL experience is collected on a 76-task subset while ERL accumulates on 244 tasks; experience budgets differ.

evidence.quote: algorithm with GPT-5-mini for up to 3 retries.
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines build experience with up to 3 Reflexion retries per task (more rollouts than ERL's single attempt).

evidence.quote: we run Reflexion with GPT-5-mini for up to 3 retries on all training tasks
evidence.support_explanation: AutoGuide experience uses retries on all training tasks.
The k=20 row of the k-sweep equals the main-result row (51.4 / 60.7 / 56.1), so retrieval count and method were compared and chosen on the same test universes.

evidence.quote: Performance exhibits a non-monotonic pattern, peaking around 40–60 heuristics before degrading with excessive inclusion.
evidence.support_explanation: Random heuristic injection already yields up to 53.8 versus 48.3 baseline.

evidence.quote: and the best random selection configuration (53.8%), confirming that retrieval quality matters more than heuristic quantity.
evidence.support_explanation: LLM retrieval 56.1 vs best random 53.8 vs embedding 53.3: retrieval adds 2.3 points over random on 76 tasks, while 5.5 of the 7.8-point gain appears with random selection.

evidence.quote: this approach fails to improve performance (-1.9% vs. baseline), suggesting that raw trajectories lack the actionable insights necessary for the agent to improve on new scenarios.
evidence.support_explanation: Few-shot raw trajectories do not help.

evidence.quote: This holds when comparing the same number of experiences provided in-context as either heuristics or raw trajectories
evidence.support_explanation: Token/experience-matched comparison supports heuristics over raw trajectories.

evidence.quote: ERL yields substantial gains on passˆ3 (+8.3% in Execution and +10.6% in Search), indicating more stable performance across runs.
evidence.support_explanation: Consistency gain over three runs; pass@3 gains small.

evidence.quote: While failure-only retrieval yields the highest overall score (58.9%), this reflects strong Search performance at the expense of Execution tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: A variant exceeds the main ERL configuration; the main configuration was not chosen by that result.

evidence.quote: Accounting for heuristic generation and retrieval, ERL incurs a 40% overall increase in API costs.
evidence.support_explanation: Total ERL evaluation cost 21.40 USD vs 15.27 USD baseline per Table 4; input tokens nearly double.

evidence.quote: shows that ERL improves overall success rate over the baseline (0.380 vs. 0.367), with gains on Airline and Retail but a slight drop on Telecom.
evidence.support_explanation: Second benchmark: +1.3 points overall with Telecom decline.

evidence.quote: The scores reveal that iterative ERL achieves higher success rates than the standard version during accumulation but lower test performance (-5.4%).
evidence.support_explanation: The online loop (retrieve while the pool grows) generalizes worse (50.7 vs 56.1); the headline result is from offline accumulation.

evidence.quote: Future work could bootstrap heuristic accumulation via synthetic task generation or address challenges in scaling heuristic pools, such as resolving conflicting guidelines and maintaining retrieval quality.
evidence.support_explanation: Pool maintenance (conflicts, consolidation, retrieval at scale) is acknowledged as unaddressed.

gap.author_gap: Agents approach each new task from scratch; prior experiential methods (ExpeL, AutoGuide) need repeated rollouts or paired trajectories, concatenate all insights into every prompt, or add per-turn retrieval overhead, which breaks down when tasks cannot be retried.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete and plausible deployment gap vs two named neighbors. The scaling-poorly and overhead claims are argued rather than measured, and the reflection-store-retrieve loop is a well-covered family whose other members (Voyager-style, memory-centric agents) are cited in a list but not compared.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion, ExpeL (insight extraction with retries), AutoGuide (context-aware guidelines), plus a cited cluster of experiential-memory works not compared.
gap.residue: Store maintenance (conflicts, consolidation), online accumulation (iterative ERL degrades), scaling retrieval beyond about 20 entries.
gap.stakes: Practical agent deployment without retries or curated training sets.
gap.method_response: Single-attempt reflection into trigger-conditioned heuristics plus LLM retrieval.
gap.remaining_gap: Maintenance, online learning, and generality beyond Gaia2 (tau2-bench shows no passˆ3 gain).
unresolved: Comparison to other experiential-memory systems at matched experience budgets

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A pool of heuristics distilled from single-attempt trajectories on 8 Gaia2 universes raises success on 2 held-out universes by about 5 to 8 points over ReAct (GPT-5-mini; 76 tasks, 3 runs), and raw few-shot trajectories do not help; the gain is not shown to beat retry-based baselines at matched experience budgets, retrieval adds about 2 points over random selection, and the online accumulation loop and the second benchmark do not reproduce the gain.
assessment.note: Author-reported results only; nothing was run by us. 'Retained' reflects held-out-universe gains from a frozen pool; no improver-level claim is made or supported.

G.reason: Concrete deployment gap relative to two named neighbors (retries and paired trajectories, all-insight prompts, per-turn retrieval); scaling and overhead criticisms are argued, not measured, and other experiential-memory neighbors are only cited.

M.reason: Mechanism and its assumptions (single-trajectory post-mortem, trigger-conditioned guideline, LLM relevance retrieval) are clear and tested against distinguishable naive alternatives (random, embedding, raw trajectories); lessons are not contrasted.

X.reason: Heuristic format, retrieval prompt, k and injection are reproducible and the reward-signal dependency is characterised, but there is no admission gate, maintenance, conflict handling or versioning, and the online loop variant degrades.

E.measurement.reason: Gaia2 scenarios have ground-truth trajectories with automatic verification and pass@3/passˆ3 are reported, though the verifier includes an LLM judge from the agent's family and the test set is only 76 tasks.

E.causality.reason: Store-off, random, embedding, raw-trajectory and success/failure controls exist, but ExpeL/AutoGuide experience budgets are unmatched, random heuristics give most of the gain, and the failures-only variant exceeds the headline without analysis.

E.holdout.reason: Accumulation and test use disjoint universes with held-out data and a second benchmark is run; k and retrieval variants were compared on the test universes and only two test universes are used.

E.statistics.reason: Three runs on 76 tasks with no variance, intervals or tests, margins of 2 points between retrieval variants, but sample sizes and several negative results (tau2 Telecom, iterative ERL, no-reward) are reported (A2 ladder level 1).

E.cost.reason: Token counts and dollar cost per phase are reported with a 40% overall increase, and a token-matched few-shot comparison is included; baseline retry costs for ExpeL/AutoGuide are not reported.

rationale: Offline reflect-and-retrieve heuristic pool (H00) with a clean held-out-universe design and honest cost and negative results. Weaknesses are unmatched ExpeL/AutoGuide budgets, test-tuned k, small test set without variance, no store maintenance, and an online variant that degrades.
